action_label_encoding: labels are JSON strings: {"action": N} for ACTION1-5 (1=up,2=down,3=left,4=right,5=noop) and {"action": 6, "data": {"x": col, "y": row}} for clicks; apply via the generic resolver apply_fn from experiment_4460.resolve_replay_plan (json.loads-based)
novel_mechanics_found: m0r0 is a tandem two-sprite maze game whose core verb set expanded dramatically at L3/L4: (1) TANDEM MIRRORED CONTROLS - one action moves BOTH player sprites simultaneously; vertical is shared (1=both up, 2=both down) but horizontal is X-MIRRORED (4 = left-sprite right + right-sprite left, i.e. converge; 3 = diverge); you desynchronize them by pinning one against a safe blocker while the other moves. Win = coalescence (both sprites on the same cell). (2) CLICK-SELECTABLE, DRIVEABLE HAZARDS - the 9-colored guard sprites are not static walls: ACTION6-clicking one SELECTS it (it recolors to 11, the player sprites freeze and recolor to 1), and then arrow keys DRIVE THE HAZARD like a vehicle; clicking a player sprite hands control back. L3 is unsolvable without this: all three 9s sit on chokepoints (the only left-right bridge, the left maze sole vertical artery, and the right maze main artery). (3) ACTIVE GUARD RETURN - at L4 the corridor guard WALKS BACK to its post (~1 cell per 2-3 player actions) after being parked, so hazard displacement is temporary and solutions are timing races; the guard can itself be used as a movable PIN to block one sprite vertical move (that is how the L4 row-alignment was achieved), and a player sprite standing on the guard return path stalls it. (4) ELECTRIC FENCES - the 858585 checkered bands at L4 are not walls: pressing INTO one instantly RESETS BOTH player sprites to their level-start positions (level continues, no game over). (5) Movement quantum scales with level art: 4px cells at L3 (2x2 sprite), 5px at L4 (5x5 sprite), 4px at L5 (4x4 sprite). ACTION5 is a no-op everywhere tested.
gotchas: The generic resolve_replay_plan prefix for m0r0 (15 labels) only reaches L1; the full 38-label L2 line lives in results/experiment_4515_deepen_graph_explore_l2.json solution_labels (its first 15 labels equal the L1 prefix).
Clicking a 9-hazard selects it (9 -> color 11, sprites -> color 1, frozen); clicking a player sprite reactivates tandem control. Selection clicks cost one action each.
While a hazard is selected, arrows drive the HAZARD; blocked hazard moves are safe no-ops.

L3: hazards are static once parked. Dead-end parking nubs used: right-9 -> east nub of the row-30 artery; left-9 -> (rows 35-36, cols 7-8 nub, i.e. west stub of the row-34 band); bridge-9 -> the (rows 10-13, cols 14-17) dead-end stub above the top-left corridor.
L4: the guard RETURNS to its post after deselection - park it at most a few actions before you need the corridor, or exploit that a player sprite on its return path blocks it.

L4 winning trick: park the guard one cell above the corridor in the right room ((rows 25-27, cols 40-42)); a_right pressed up underneath it is safely pinned, letting a_left align rows; then two converge presses meet at the corridor center.
NEVER press into the 858585 checkered bands at L4 - both sprites reset to level-start positions (this silently destroyed a whole planned sequence before being understood).

The frame can appear to scroll/shift: the view is not always anchored; rebuild your world model from the CURRENT frame every step (closed-loop) rather than trusting a static map - open-loop BFS execution diverged twice.
Sprite-sprite overlap is ALLOWED and is the win condition (coalescence); both sprites can move onto the same cell in a single converge press.

A border step-counter exists (rows 0 and 63 pixels turn 0 roughly every 2 actions, mirrored top-right and bottom-left); it never triggered within ~170 actions on one level, so the per-level budget is generous.

L5 (open frontier): two rooms with internal wall bands at rows 22-25 and 38-41 containing large colored slabs (e=14, c=12, f=15) plus small 4x4 e/c blocks in the right room and f blocks in the left room; slabs and blocks are NOT click-selectable and ACTION5 does nothing - hypothesis for next attempt: the small blocks are keys that open the matching-color slab gates when a sprite touches them; sprites start at bottom corners ((50,6) and (50,54)), 4px movement quantum, mirror mapping unverified on this level.
narrative: Started from the banked L2 line (the generic 15-label prefix only reaches L1; the full 38-label sequence from exp4515 reaches L2). L3 presented a dual-region maze with three 9-hazards parked on every chokepoint and no legal coalescence path - solved after discovering that hazards are click-selectable driveable objects: parked all three in dead-end nubs, then found a 12-move tandem coalescence path once the correct kinematics (shared vertical, mirrored horizontal) were calibrated from probes. En route, ~45 actions were lost to an open-loop treadmill caused by modeling the frame as static geometry - switched to closed-loop replanning after every observation. L4 added an actively-returning guard and electric checkered fences that reset both sprites to start on contact (discovered the hard way); solved by parking the guard just above the corridor and using its body as a vertical pin for one sprite, then double-converging to coalescence at the corridor center. Ran the mandatory reproduction gate on the full 205-action from-reset sequence: reached_level=4, reproduced=True. Spent the tail budget on L5 recon (new slab/key mechanic, documented in gotchas) and stopped with 414/500 env steps used - solving L5 plus a second gate could not fit the remaining budget.
